title: Create a running record of your team's strategic decisions
description: A system that turns meeting transcripts into a searchable log of what your team decided, who owns it, and what's still open.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

personal-knowledge-base.title: Personal Knowledge Base
personal-knowledge-base.content: A store of your own accumulated knowledge — notes, decisions, references — organized so an AI can search and use it. The difference from a pile of documents: structure and maintenance. Level 2 builds one as a wiki.

children.text: Oracle research cited in [Deloitte's 2026 Global Human Capital Trends](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/topics/talent/human-capital-trends/2026/decision-making-with-ai.html) found 72% of leaders say data overload and a lack of trust in their own data has stalled decisions entirely. Much of that is a memory problem. This system reads a meeting transcript or your notes and adds one entry to a running decision log, naming what was decided, who owns it, the deadline, and what's still open.
As AI takes on more of the analysis behind a decision, the paper trail of what a team committed to becomes the thing that stops settled questions from getting reopened.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) right after any meeting that ends in a real call, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill) your whole team can invoke, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that pulls from your meeting notetaker on its own. Every version writes into your existing [knowledge base](#tooltip-personal-knowledge-base) rather than a new tool to check.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming which meetings feed the log, where the record lives, what counts as a real decision, and who can search it.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns our meeting transcripts and notes into a running record of the strategic decisions we've made. Ask me questions, one at a time, about which meetings should feed this, where the record should live, what counts as a real decision versus just a discussion, and who needs to be able to search it later. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview forces you to define "a real decision" before the tool ever sees a transcript, so the log doesn't fill up with things that were only discussed.

items: Where the record itself lives and who can search it.
Whether it's fed from raw transcripts or from someone's cleaned-up notes.
How far back you backfill versus starting fresh from today.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common connectors are your meeting notetaker (Fathom, Otter, Fireflies) for the transcript, your knowledge base ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Confluence) to host the log, and your task tracker (Asana, Linear) if an owner needs a linked task. The paste-in version needs none.

**Create.** Start building the system your scope document describes, and test it on a real transcript or a fresh set of notes. The prompt below is an example. Your scope document will give you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Extract the actual decisions from this meeting transcript and add them to our running decision log.

Context: Here's the transcript or notes: [paste]. Our log format tracks: date, decision, owner, deadline, and open questions.

Rules:
- Only log something as a decision if the group committed to it, not if it was floated or debated without resolution.
- Separate decisions from action items, they're not the same thing.
- Flag anything that sounded like a decision but had no clear owner assigned.
- Output in a format I can paste directly into [Notion / a spreadsheet].
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: separating decisions from action items keeps the log from filling with tasks, and the missing-owner flag catches decisions that would otherwise quietly die for lack of an owner.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Real decisions only, owners flagged when missing, format ready to paste in?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what it missed or over-logged, and fold the correction into the rules.

items: Connect it through a [tool connector](#tooltip-tool-connectors) so entries log right after each meeting.
Add a quarterly review pass that surfaces decisions nobody followed up on.
Build a check that flags when a new decision contradicts a past one.
Tag decisions by initiative so a new hire can read one project's history.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat draft the rubric and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each decision-log entry, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for meeting date, decisions logged, decisions missing an owner, decisions later contradicted, and what I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call on what counts as a decision, and the log columns surface missing owners and contradictions after a few weeks of entries.

children.text: **Log** every entry against the rubric. Note the date and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from the log. Once the rubric passes a few weeks straight, package the prompt and rules into a reusable AI skill. A repeated miss is your next candidate. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill interviews you and writes it; a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. It can't tell a real decision from a discussion unless you draw that line for it, so don't let it fill in an owner or a deadline that was never assigned.
